correctness.rationale: Both graph constructions have 4+r+K vertices where K=max(100,4r+10): a remote path of length q=r+K versus a length-(r+1) stem entering a terminal K-clique. The radius-r marked balls have the same degree labels, and u-c-v are bridge links giving R_uv=2. Reconstructing the published cut-vertex Poisson-excursion transfer with artificial remote completion time T, its Laplace transforms a=E exp(-T), b=E exp(-3T/2) and unused suffix J yields delta=2ET-2(2m-1)(a-2b/3)-2E[J(exp(-T)-exp(-3T/2))]. For the long path, ET=q and J=q^2 reduce to the strictly positive rational function 2(6q^3+5q^2-23q-10)/(3(q+1)(3q+2)). For the terminal clique, a single excursion covers the clique with conditional probability >1/2 when K>=100; thinning gives ET<=2(r+1) and a>=1/(2r+3). The negative bound follows from K(K-1)>12r^2+28r+11, verified symbolically from K>=4r+10. Independent exact visited-subset Bellman calculations reproduce strict signs on (r,K)=(1,3),(1,4),(2,4); these are finite corroborations only.
